title: Chicken Licken
strapline: The sky is falling! Or is it just an acorn?
intent: A tale about a panic that spreads opens gentle talk about jumping to conclusions, checking facts and staying calm.
The chain of rhyming names — Henny Penny, Cocky Locky, Ducky Lucky — is a joyful mouthful that plays with sound and rhythm.
Sequencing the growing crowd of animals off to tell the king is early ordering and counting.
The sly fox at the end links to talk about who to trust and thinking before we follow the crowd.
The story is a lively small world for journeying, gathering and acting out.
implementation: Set out Chicken Licken and the rhyming-named animals, a path to the king, an acorn and a fox's den.
Tell the story with relish for the silly names, then let children chant them and take the parts.
Wonder together: 'Was the sky really falling? What actually hit Chicken Licken on the head?'
Sequence the growing crowd: 'Who joined next? How many animals are off to see the king now?'
Open the thinking talk: 'Should they have believed him without checking? What could they have done?'
Follow the play — children love the rhyming names and the panic, and adding their own animals to the line.
key_questions: Was the sky really falling — how could they have checked?
Who joined the crowd next — can you say all their names?
How many animals are going to tell the king now?
Why was it a bad idea to follow the fox?
What should Chicken Licken have done first?

impact.text: Children play with the rhyming names and enjoy the sound and rhythm.
Children sequence and count the growing crowd of animals.
Children talk about checking before believing and thinking before following.
Children talk about the fox's trick and who to trust.
Children act out the journey together with roles and shared ideas.

enhancements: A story trail with the animals to gather one by one on the way to the king.
A rhyming-name matching game — pairing each animal with its silly rhyme.
Acorns and a 'what really fell?' investigation tray.
Masks or puppets of the animals for retelling and taking parts.
A calm-down corner talk about checking facts before we worry.

playing_exploring: Children relish the silly rhyming names and act out the panic with glee.
They gather the animals and travel the story their own way.
active_learning: Children keep the growing chain of characters going all the way to the king.
They take on the parts and see the shared retelling through.
creating_thinking: Children reason about whether the sky was really falling and how to check.
They work out why following the fox was a mistake.
